summary: The Witcher franchise entries added as supplemental sourced guide rows; Sami did not list these in the locked personal spine.

entries.title: The Witcher: Crimson Trail

emulation.notes: Use only if original hardware is unavailable; document emulator and build.

primary.why: The Witcher: Crimson Trail was a 2007 mobile-phone action RPG spin-off released for legacy mobile/J2ME devices. No later official port is sourced, so the original mobile release is the archival route.
primary.how_to_play: Use a preserved legacy mobile build on compatible hardware or a J2ME preservation setup, documenting exact build/device details.

entries.remaster_caveats: Legacy mobile spin-off; no modern official port is sourced.

entries.title: The Witcher
entries.definitive_edition: Enhanced Edition Director's Cut on Windows

primary.why: The Witcher released for Windows in 2007 and later for OS X, while the planned console remake Rise of the White Wolf was canceled. Windows Enhanced Edition Director's Cut is the best archive route because it is the updated official PC edition with well-documented fixes and the strongest capture path.
primary.how_to_play: Use The Witcher: Enhanced Edition Director's Cut on Windows through GOG or Steam with current compatibility fixes.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Witcher Remake is a future separate project and should not replace this entry until it ships.

entries.title: The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings

primary.why: The Witcher 2 released on Windows, Xbox 360, OS X, and Linux. Windows Enhanced Edition is the best archive route because it has the strongest capture/settings ceiling and the complete enhanced content path.
primary.how_to_play: Use The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings Enhanced Edition on Windows through GOG or Steam, applying known fixes if needed.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later official remaster is sourced.

entries.title: The Witcher Adventure Game

primary.why: The Witcher Adventure Game received a digital adaptation for OS X, Windows, Android, and iOS. Windows is the best archive route because it has the best display/capture path for the digital board-game adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows digital version if owned; otherwise preserve the physical board game separately outside this video-game archive.

entries.remaster_caveats: Digital adaptation of the tabletop board game; physical board game is outside this video-game entry.

entries.title: The Witcher Battle Arena

emulation.notes: Service shutdown limits preservation to captures/metadata.

primary.why: The Witcher Battle Arena was a mobile MOBA released for Android, iOS, and Windows Phone, but its servers closed at the end of 2015. The Android/iOS launch build is the archival reference, not a normal current play route.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is sourced; preserve legacy captures, client metadata, and server-shutdown history.

entries.remaster_caveats: Servers closed on December 31, 2015; no official offline edition is sourced.

entries.title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
entries.definitive_edition: Complete Edition with next-generation update on Windows

primary.why: The Witcher 3 released on PlayStation 4, Windows, and Xbox One, then came to Switch and received a next-generation update for Windows, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. Windows Complete Edition is the best archive route because it includes Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, supports the next-gen update, and has the highest graphics/mod/capture ceiling.
primary.how_to_play: Use The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Complete Edition on Windows with the next-generation update. Revisit after the announced Songs of the Past expansion ships.

entries.remaster_caveats: Next-generation update changed rendering/features; future Songs of the Past expansion is not part of the current shipped Complete Edition state.

entries.title: Gwent: The Witcher Card Game

primary.why: Gwent released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, iOS, Android, and macOS, with console support later discontinued. Windows is the best archive route because it is the main PC version with the strongest display/capture path and post-console service continuity.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows version. Verify current community-balance/service state before capture.

entries.remaster_caveats: Official support entered maintenance/community-balance mode; verify service state before capture.

entries.title: Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales

primary.why: Thronebreaker released on Windows, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, iOS, and Android. Windows is the best archive route because it has the highest display/capture ceiling for the standalone single-player campaign.
primary.how_to_play: Use the current Windows version through GOG or Steam.

entries.remaster_caveats: Standalone single-player Gwent-based RPG, not a Witcher 3 expansion.

entries.title: The Witcher: Monster Slayer

emulation.notes: Service shutdown limits preservation to captures/metadata.

primary.why: Monster Slayer released for Android and iOS as a geolocation AR mobile game and was shut down in 2023. The original mobile release is the archival reference, but there is no normal current play route.
primary.how_to_play: No current official play route is sourced; preserve legacy captures, client metadata, and shutdown history.

entries.remaster_caveats: Game was shut down in 2023; no official offline edition is sourced.

entries.title: Gwent: Rogue Mage
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release, edition documented at time of capture

primary.why: Gwent: Rogue Mage released for Windows, iOS, and Android as a standalone single-player expansion to Gwent. Windows is the best archive route because it has the best display/capture ceiling, though store availability changed after the Deluxe Edition removal.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows version if owned or currently available through an official storefront; document edition and storefront because Deluxe Edition availability changed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Deluxe Edition removal dates exist; verify current standard/owned access before capture.

entries.title: Roach Race

primary.why: Roach Race is a free-to-play sidescroller released for iOS and Android, with an embedded arcade-minigame version in Cyberpunk 2077. The standalone mobile release is the cleanest Witcher-franchise archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Use the standalone iOS or Android release if available; capture the Cyberpunk 2077 embedded version separately only for comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Also exists as a Cyberpunk 2077 arcade minigame; keep that as a comparison route.

entries.title: Reigns: The Witcher

primary.why: Reigns: The Witcher released in 2026 for PC/Mac and mobile platforms. Windows is the best archive route because it has the strongest capture/display path for the new Witcher/Reigns crossover.
primary.how_to_play: Use the Windows release through Steam or GOG; mobile versions are convenient secondary ownership routes but not needed for exclusive content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Crossover spin-off in the Reigns format, not a mainline action RPG.

entries.title: The Witcher IV

primary.platform: Unreleased - PlayStation 5 / Windows / Xbox Series X/S listed
primary.why: The Witcher IV is in development, targeting PlayStation 5, Windows, and Xbox Series X/S, but no released build is available for fidelity/completeness analysis.
primary.how_to_play: Do not archive a play route until the game ships and final platform behavior is verified.

entries.remaster_caveats: Future mainline title; revisit after launch.

entries.title: The Witcher Remake

primary.why: CD Projekt Red announced The Witcher Remake as a ground-up Unreal Engine 5 remake developed with Fool's Theory, but no public shipped platform/build set is available for best-version analysis.
primary.how_to_play: Do not archive a play route until the remake ships and final platform behavior is verified.

entries.remaster_caveats: Future remake; do not replace the 2007 Enhanced Edition entry until it ships.
